messages:
Alex (Support): Hey team — multiple customers reporting 5xx / timeouts hitting the hosted text-generation endpoints since ~03:10 UTC. Sample request IDs: req_8a3f, req_8a4a, req_8b01. They see 502/504 and long wait times before gateway closes. Customers include acme-inc and shopsoft. Escalating to eng-oncall.

Sophia (CS): acme sent curl logs and a stack trace. They call /v1/generate with model:redwood-ggml and often get a timeout after ~12s. They said this started right after your deploy earlier this morning. Customer is pretty upset (sla risk).

Leo (Oncall): @Marta can you take a look at the kv/cache layer? This smells like our prefix caching path failing (we had that rollout queued). Any errors in memcached/redis?

Marta (Eng Runtime): Looking at grafana — spike in 5xx for route /v1/generate around 03:12. Also seeing error bursts from service `prefix-kv-proxy` complaining about connection resets. I pulled logs from the cache pods:

```
2026-03-15T03:12:24Z ERROR prefix-kv-proxy: memcached: connection refused
2026-03-15T03:12:24Z WARN  prefix-kv-proxy: failed get cache key "prefix:session:...": EOF
2026-03-15T03:12:25Z ERROR prefix-kv-proxy: redis: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
2026-03-15T03:12:26Z ERROR prefix-kv-proxy: upstream timeout to runtime shard /generate
```

Marta (Eng Runtime): Seems like two problems: memcached cluster had an eviction storm connection issue and our redis cluster hit maxmemory and started rejecting writes/reads. Both cause the prefix cache path to hang and our gateway waits then returns 502/504.

Leo (Oncall): That aligns with the customer errors. PagerDuty alert fired for cache cluster and a Redis high memory alarm. Any recent deploys? @DeployBot any deploys around 03:10?

DeployBot: deploy/redwood-inference@prod roll-forward by mgarcia completed at 03:08 UTC. Change: enable prefix caching for multi-tenant route via feature flag `enable_prefix_cache=true` AND bump cache TTL default.

Alex (Support): ok so rollout + cache clusters stressed. Customers need immediate mitigation — can we bypass the prefix cache on traffic to hosted API so requests go directly to runtime (no cache) until we stabilize?

Marta (Eng Runtime): Yes. We have a quick kill-switch in the control plane. Two options: A) flip feature flag to false to disable prefix cache across the fleet, or B) flip the gateway rule to send a header `x-cache-bypass:true` for all hosted-inference traffic. Option A is fastest.

Leo (Oncall): Steps I'll run now:
1) curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/flags/enable_prefix_cache" -d '{"value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN'
2) kubectl rollout restart deployment/prefix-kv-proxy -n inference (if any pods stuck)
3) scale up redis nodes if needed: terraform apply -target=module.redis.cluster.number_nodes=5 (last-resort)

Marta (Eng Runtime): Before scaling, try the feature flag flip. Also start a memcached rolling restart to clear connections: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/memcached -n infra-cache`

Leo (Oncall): flipping flag now...

RedisBot: ALERT: redis-cluster-prod: maxmemory reached at 98% (03:14 UTC). Eviction policy: volatile-lru.

Leo (Oncall): flag flipped to false. Observing gateway traffic...

~ 90s later ~

Marta (Eng Runtime): Early signs look good — 5xx count falling, latency back to normal for some clients. Logs show fewer connection errors. Memcached still flaky but not causing tail errors now.

Alex (Support): I told acme and shopsoft we're patching and asked them to retry. They retried with a couple of sample req IDs and reported success. One of them still saw a 502 on a retry but subsequent attempts succeeded.

Sophia (CS): Acme appreciated the quick response. They asked for a postmortem and to know if we will revert the flag or roll a safer rollout path.

Marta (Eng Runtime): We should keep the prefix cache disabled until we repro and fix root causes: memcached connection churn (proxy bug with connection pooling) and redis memory pressure from an unexpected TTL bump. Action items I propose:
- Reproduce locally with load test and confirm memcached connection leak in prefix-kv-proxy.
- Revert TTL bump and audit any TTL/size changes in the last deploy.
- Add circuit-breaker and faster fail-open path in prefix-kv-proxy so it returns cache-miss quickly instead of blocking.
- Add better metrics: per-key TTL distribution and cache rejection rates.

Leo (Oncall): Agree. I'll keep the flag off for now and schedule a canary with strict limits once fixes are in. Opening an incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem.

Alex (Support): Customers asked for a reproducible tip: if they see the 5xx, they can set header `x-bypass-cache:true` in the meantime to avoid transient cache errors. Example: `curl -H "x-bypass-cache:true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate` — we verified that succeeded for acme.

Marta (Eng Runtime): I'll also push a short-lived hotfix to prefix-kv-proxy: fix connection pool backoff and cap outstanding requests to cache to avoid head-of-line blocking. Will request a canary to 5% traffic and watch metrics.

DeployBot: hotfix branch `fix/prefix-pool` built and awaiting review.

Sophia (CS): Please tag me when the postmortem is ready; acme wants an ETA and steps to avoid future customer impact.

Leo (Oncall): Incident ticket created: INC-2026-324. Owner: Marta (Eng Runtime). Keeping channel updated.

Alex (Support): Thanks team — I'll follow up with each customer and include workaround header. Putting this thread in watchlist. :thumbsup:

Marta (Eng Runtime): Quick follow-up note for the postmortem: we discovered that the TTL bump was accidental (config drift in a feature branch). We'll include a timeline and the exact commands used to flip the flag and the kubectl restarts.

Leo (Oncall): Closing loop later today after canary. If anyone sees residual 5xx please @oncall immediately.

RedisBot: RESOLVED: redis-cluster-prod memory usage stabilized after cache TTL revert and subsequent restart (03:45 UTC).

Alex (Support): Marking customer tickets as updated. Will post postmortem link here when it's published.

(End of thread)
